newsitem.title: CANADA: S.Africa's Stals sees need for economic reform.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Stals sees need for economic reform.

text.p: Chris Stals, governor of the South Africa Reserve Bank, said on Friday that South Africa's government was implementing reforms aimed at economic liberalization, but he cited several inherent weaknesses in the country's current economic structure.

He told an audience at the 39th annual congress of the Association Cambiste Internationale that South Africa remained heavily dependent on foreign investment capital and has made little progress addressing urgent unemployment problems.
"The best estimates available indicate that at this stage about 30 percent of the economic active population of the country is unemployed," Stals said.

He also expressed concern about the low level of the country's official foreign exchange reserves, which he said made South Africa "vulnerable to current account deficits in an environment of volatile international capital movements."
Stals said these economic deficiencies required incisive structural adjustment, which would not be possible without "painful reform."

Outside the economic arena, Stals said that escalating crime and violence, and the presence of wasteful corruption in the public and private sectors are important concerns that the government must address.
